---
title: "Software"
---

I build open-source tools for research methods, reproducible workflows, and
statistical reporting. These projects contribute to my emerging
[Computational Credibility research program](research.qmd#computational-credibility)
by making computational methods and workflows more transparent and open to
evaluation. Development stages and current capabilities vary by package.

## mlmr

`mlmr` is an R package and Shiny app for fitting, understanding, and reporting
mixed-effects and multilevel models. It is designed for researchers,
instructors, graduate students, and applied analysts who want a guided
model-building workflow without giving up transparent R code.

The app uses `lme4` under the hood and supports model setup, centering choices,
fixed and random effects, interaction terms, APA-style tables, equations,
diagnostics, and reproducible exports.

- [Open the mlmr documentation site](https://marcusharrisphd.com/mlmr/)
- [View the GitHub repository](https://github.com/MarcusHarrisUConn/mlmr)
- [Report issues or give beta feedback](https://github.com/MarcusHarrisUConn/mlmr/issues)

```r
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("MarcusHarrisUConn/mlmr")
mlmr::run_mlmr()
```

## mcsimr

*Monte Carlo simulation design and reporting | Early development*

`mcsimr` is an R package and Shiny workbench for designing, running, and
reporting Monte Carlo simulation studies in the social and behavioral sciences.
Its main focus is structural equation modeling with `lavaan`, with OLS
regression available as a simpler starting point.

Researchers can vary population parameters, sample sizes, estimators,
missing-data mechanisms, and distributional conditions, then examine
performance measures such as bias, coverage, power, and convergence.
The workflow supports reproducible R code, parallel execution, checkpoints,
and Quarto exports with tables, figures, and reporting materials. The package
is under active development, and its API may evolve.

- [View the GitHub repository and documentation](https://github.com/MarcusHarrisUConn/mcsimr)
- [Report issues or give feedback](https://github.com/MarcusHarrisUConn/mcsimr/issues)

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("MarcusHarrisUConn/mcsimr")
mcsimr::use_mcsimr_app()
```

## DSEMr

*Dynamic structural equation modeling | Experimental foundation release*

`DSEMr` is an R package under active development for dynamic structural
equation modeling. It aims to support transparent, reproducible workflows for
studying time-series relations within people and variation across people,
including methodological research and Monte Carlo studies.

The current estimation scope covers Gaussian AR(1) models for a single time
series, with optional contemporaneous covariates, and an experimental two-level
Gaussian AR(1) model using an R reference engine. The package combines a
`lavaan`-inspired model language with a Rust numerical backend. Broader latent,
categorical, and other DSEM model families remain development targets; this
release is not a general replacement for Mplus.

- [View the GitHub repository and documentation](https://github.com/MarcusHarrisUConn/DSEMr)
- [View the current model support and validation roadmap](https://github.com/MarcusHarrisUConn/DSEMr/blob/main/docs/PARITY.md)
- [Report issues or give feedback](https://github.com/MarcusHarrisUConn/DSEMr/issues)

Source installation requires R 4.2 or later and a Rust toolchain with Cargo.

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("MarcusHarrisUConn/DSEMr")
```
